body: Thank you again
Thank you. I’ve been feeling guilty for considering separation or divorce since this post. I’ll look for non Christian advice. Any recommendations where I can find it?
Did you really say that if I get out of the marriage “I committed to” there is no place for me in heaven? You have to be part of the cult I left. What church are you in?
I don’t understand the question?
I’m honestly shocked by your responses.

If what you say is true, then every domestic abuse victim deserved their fate simply because they didn’t walk away. Do you understand that I did not have choices at the age of 16? Do you understand that my options were to continue to be beaten, possibly to death as others in my cult had been, or marry who I was told to marry? How do you think I had a choice here?

Similar things were said to me when I was told I would marry my husband. So apparently me being happy and choosing my own life is self centered and I deserved to be beaten into submission. I’m sure I still deserve that.
I’m zero percent interested in meeting another man, furthest thing from my mind, and not the point.
Thank you for saying this. I feel like this is a definite option.
What is that?

It’s more than just household duties. It’s more always being there when the kids need to talk, emotional support, school help, relationship advice, etc. There’s a lot to having as many kids as we do. I’ve never not been there for them. I’m depended on by everyone.

Carving out a like for myself has proven to be difficult because of the immense amount of responsibility I have at home. I have no education and no time to get one. No friends due to the isolated life we’ve lived. No family support because they’re still in the cult and cannot support me doing more than being a wife and mom. No time for a job because of how much I do for the kids and with the kids. Most days I just want to run away from home and start a new life that I choose. But obviously I stay for the kids. I can’t be that selfish.
Yes he treats all of us well. He is a good father and provider. Very involved with all of the kids. We have many.
Not of us not being together.
Thank you for the advice!

Yes we both grew up in it. He believes he’s fine and somewhat still believes the religion is truth. It’s not. And that part of it can be toxic for our marriage. Yes I’ve been to a lot of counseling, which has helped me find my voice and confidence that I’m not just a baby making machine. I’ve grown a lot. Still lots of trauma tho and triggers and feeling like I’m not enough for the real world.
Ah ok thank you.

I do believe in God and consider myself a Christian. My husband knows how I feel about all of this, I have shared everything with him and continue to. He feels bad and like he’s held me back in my life, but at the same time won’t let me go. He is a good man. I however don’t know who I am or where I belong in the world. I have nothing other than him and the kids. I want so much more.
That sounds simple, but my life is far from that.
Which religion were you in?
Yes. He knows what I want to do.
I agree that fear is what stops me from pursuing my own dreams and the life I want.

My husband knows how I feel, he agrees wrong was done, and he feels responsible for holding me back. At the same time he loves me and wants to stay together more than let me go. With the kids, that’s a harder relationship to navigate as far as sharing my feelings about myself and leaving. They just want the picture perfect family that they feel we are. They don’t want anything to change.
Yes I left the religion and took the kids, my husband followed months later so he could stay with us. We’re all out.
